reviews.summary: Under the Cloudflare-primitive-correctness lens, the invariant sweep largely held. All eight named focus sections comply with the trust_grade sidecar-only rule: §3.2/§5.2 (canonical) keep trust_grade out of the Vectorize metadata-index list and the upsert blob, LEFT-JOINed from memory_use_policy at hydration; §5.3.2 hydrates trust_grade via getChunksByIds and runs the boost post-hydration; §7.4 omits trust_grade from create-metadata-index; §7.5 states "trust grade feeds search ranking (not isolation)"; §8.3's embed-everything metadata blob is {userId,teamId,scope,sessionId,visibility,embedding_model} with no trust_grade; §10.4/§10.6/§10.7 provision only scope/team_id/visibility/embedding_model. brain-entities is declared in EVERY env binding block (§10.1 top-level vectorize[], §10.2 staging AND production) and provisioned in §10.4 (+§10.7 deploy runbook) with the same four metadata indexes and no trust_grade. api_keys.allowed_scopes alignment is solid and consistent: mint-time intersect(requestedGrant, minter.allowedScopes), NULL='*' iff minter was '*', resolved into Principal.allowedScopes, escalation path closed (§7.1/§7.2/§7.10). Affirmed CF-correctness strength: the query sets returnMetadata:'indexed' (not 'all') and never returnValues:true, so the topK=100 ceiling holds even with a metadata filter — the §5.3.2 recall-cliff claim is sound. Vectorize V2 supports $in/$nin, so the canonical {scope:{$in:[...]}} single-query path in §5.3.2 is correct. Remaining defects are textual/contract consistency, not isolation breaks or nonexistent-primitive requirements: (1) six code-reference/architecture prose lines still direct the implementer to "move trust_grade to filterable metadata," contradicting canonical §3.2 sidecar-only — high because they are directive and the focus said "anywhere," but trust_grade is ranking-only so it cannot leak; (2) §7.3 foldPartitionFilter code returns single-scope only and its comment says "caller fans out per-scope, then union," contradicting canonical §5.3.2's single-query {scope:{$in:[...]}} — since $in is real, §7.3 is the stale side; (3) §7.3 code comment "visibility='world' is pushed when its index is live" and §3.2 line 1062 "visibility='world' is folded into the metadata filter" contradict §5.3.2's explicit, well-argued "visibility is NOT pushed"; entity-arm prose (§6.6/§6.7/§9) says visibility IS folded — reconcilable (KG node space is {world,team} only, no own-private entity to lose) but the asymmetry rationale is unstated. None caps below 60; the isolation core is sound. Score 64, consistent with the prior 68 ceiling minus the trust_grade-prose drift and foldPartitionFilter contract divergence.

reviews.summary: Post-sweep re-score on the requirements-coverage / internal-consistency lens. All three targeted invariants are genuinely resolved with no surviving contradiction. (1) trust_grade is sidecar-only everywhere: absent from the chunks DDL (§3.1.1/§4.9) and facts DDL (§3.1.6); CHECK-constrained only on memory_use_policy (§3.1.5); explicitly excluded from Vectorize metadata and not a metadata index (§3.2/§4.9); written only via insertUsePolicy in the promote batch (§8.3) and updateUsePolicy on promotion (§7.5); read via LEFT JOIN + COALESCE(...,'evidence') (§5.2/§5.3). (2) brain-entities is provisioned in the top-level vectorize block AND in both staging and production env blocks (§10.1/§10.2); dev = top-level config, so all three environments carry ENTITY_INDEX — the prior contradiction is fixed. (3) api_keys.allowed_scopes is defined (§3.1.4 DDL, §7.1 Drizzle), written via the mint-time intersect(requestedGrant, minter.allowedScopes) rule (consistent prose at §7.1/§7.10), and read in the bk_ branch (§7.2) and §9.0.1 step 3 — the two-axis allowedScopes(data)/capabilities(capability) split is consistent across §1.4/§7.2/§9.0.1/§9.0.2 with no residual single-scopes collapse. Score lifts above the prior 68 because the invariant sweep landed; held out of the 80s by one in-scope medium (a membership-SQL divergence between §9.0.1 and §7.2) plus two low documentation gaps. No unresolved critical, so no sub-60 cap applies.

strengths: api_keys.allowed_scopes is a real, dual-defined (§3.1.4 DDL + §7.1 Drizzle) column, written at mint as intersect(requestedGrant, minter.allowedScopes) and read at resolve in the §7.2 bk_ branch with fail-closed parseScopeGrant→[]; a restricted minter can never widen to '*' and a restricted key never resolves to '*' (one-step escalation closed, §7.10).

trust_grade is authoritatively sidecar-only: NOT a Vectorize metadata index and NOT in the upsert blob (§3.2 line 1061, §1.4 line 1543); foldPartitionFilter folds ONLY scope/visibility and the trust boost runs post-hydration on the LEFT-JOINed memory_use_policy value — no cross-grade leak via metadata is possible, and a promotion never re-upserts a vector.

The entity search arm (search_entities) carries the SAME tenant+scope+visibility gate as the chunk arm: namespace=tenantId, scope+{world,team} folded into the metadata filter, then authoritative D1 re-check on entities (scopePredicate + {world,team} visibilityPredicate); entities are scope-partitioned in the dedup key (§6.1) so the same name under two clients is two rows, and the gate columns physically exist on the entities table.

Break-glass over private memory is fail-closed and audited by construction (§7.6): role-gated to owner/admin, 403 for any non-admin signal incl. breakGlass:true, tenant_id hard boundary never bypassed, breakglass_read audit row written in the same db.batch plus a guaranteed alert; canaries #14/#15 assert both the deny path and the audited allow path.

Intra-tenant RLS (visibilityPredicate) is a structural Scoped* contract, not per-op prose: ScopedDB.readFacts and getChunksByIds/hydrateChunks always AND (world OR team∈teamIds OR private∧user_id=self), the chunks table carries visibility/user_id/team_id (§3.1.1), session chunks inherit session visibility while ingested docs default world, and a table-driven canary meta-test fails if a new read surface skips the choke-point.

Defense-in-depth on both search arms: the FTS arm enforces c.scope IN(grants) inline AND drops out-of-grant ids at scope-gated hydration; the vector arm hard-wires namespace=tenantId and re-checks every id at the D1 gate, so a forgotten/forged Vectorize filter or a missing metadata index cannot leak another scope or tenant.

weaknesses.issue: Internal contradiction at the isolation boundary on the doc/entity LINK arm. §7.3's getLinks (2947-2953) and expandFrontier (2955-2960) gate via scopePredicate2(docLinks.scope) — but doc_links (§6.1, 2127-2138) and entity_relations (§6.1, 2212-2222) have NO scope column; the edge DDL carries only tenant_id + from/to ids + link_type/context. These methods also do NO node JOIN and return raw edge rows. Yet §6.1/§2110 (iter-4 fix) and Flow C (§6.7 line 2546) require the NODE-level scopePredicate+visibilityPredicate applied to JOINed pages/entities endpoints. As literally coded in §7.3, get_links/get_backlinks are gated on tenant_id + a phantom column only, so a restricted Persona-C principal (allowedScopes=['clientA']) can enumerate edge rows (from_id/to_id/link_type/context text) touching clientB-scope or team/private pages within the same tenant — a cross-scope/visibility intra-tenant leak sitting inside the §7.3 choke-point itself. Cross-tenant still holds (tenant_id always applied).
weaknesses.recommendation: Resolve the contradiction toward Flow C / §2110: rewrite getLinks/expandFrontier (and get_backlinks) to JOIN each edge endpoint to its node table (pages/entities) and AND nodeGate(spec, nf)+nodeGate(spec, nt) — the exact gate traverse() already uses — instead of the nonexistent docLinks.scope/entity_relations.scope predicate. Delete scopePredicate2(docLinks.scope) and scopePredicate2(entity_relations.scope). Ensure get_links/get_backlinks return endpoint-hydrated, node-gated results, not raw edge rows. Add a canary asserting get_links/get_backlinks (not just traverse_graph) drop edges whose far endpoint is out-of-scope or team/private.

weaknesses.issue: Stale, self-contradictory prose in §7.4 (line 3126): 'Once graph nodes carry a visibility column, the visibilityPredicate rides along too; until then, discovered ids are re-hydrated...'. But §6.1 and §2110 (iter-4) ALREADY add the visibility column to pages and entities and mandate the node-level visibility gate on the graph arm. So §7.4 describes a pre-iter-4 world where node visibility is not yet enforced and re-hydration is the only safety net — directly contradicting §6.1/§2108-2110. A reader/implementer following §7.4 would build the weaker re-hydration-only path and skip the node visibility gate on traversal/links.
weaknesses.recommendation: Update §7.4 to state unconditionally that pages/entities carry visibility (§6.1) and that every graph frontier/link read ANDs the node-level scopePredicate+visibilityPredicate via nodeGate on the JOINed endpoints. Remove the 'until then' conditional and the implication that re-hydration is the primary graph-arm visibility gate (it is now belt-and-suspenders, not the boundary).

weaknesses.issue: Doc-hygiene inconsistency the invariant sweep missed: §1.5 (line 97), §2 (lines 354), §1.4 (line 1543 header text) and several code-reference lines (541, 1602, 2081, 3326) still describe trust_grade as pushed 'to metadata' / 'trust_grade as metadata filters' within the Vectorize namespace. This contradicts the authoritative §3.2 (line 1061) and §5.2/§5.3, which state trust_grade is deliberately NOT a Vectorize metadata index and NOT in the upsert blob. Not an isolation leak (trust_grade affects ranking only, and foldPartitionFilter folds only scope/visibility), but an implementer following the §1.5/§2 prose could wrongly add trust_grade as filterable metadata, wasting a scarce index slot and producing stale values on every promotion.
weaknesses.recommendation: Scrub the residual 'trust_grade to metadata'/'as metadata filters' phrasing in §1.5 line 97, §2 line 354, the code-reference lines (541, 1602, 2081, 3326), and the §1.4 line 1543 description so they all match the authoritative §3.2: trust_grade lives only in memory_use_policy, LEFT-JOINed at read, never a Vectorize filter.

weaknesses.issue: nodeGate/nodeVisible/resolveScopedNode build raw SQL by string-interpolating EdgeSpec field names (${alias}.${spec.scopeCol}, ${spec.nodeTable}, ${spec.visibilityCol}) into the query (lines 2974-3028). EdgeSpec is a static internal constant (DOC_GRAPH/ENTITY_GRAPH), so there is no current injection vector, but this is the one place in the isolation choke-point that constructs identifiers via template strings rather than the parameterized binds used elsewhere. If a future EdgeSpec ever became config- or caller-derived, the scope/visibility gate would become injectable.
weaknesses.recommendation: Add an explicit invariant/comment that EdgeSpec values are compile-time constants only and must never be sourced from request input, and/or validate spec column/table names against an allowlist before interpolation. Keep the binds (already used for the scope/team/user values) and never interpolate values, only the vetted identifiers.

reviews.summary: From the multi-tenant + intra-tenant isolation lens, three of the four checkpoints are now genuinely closed and the invariant sweep largely held. (1) api_keys.allowed_scopes is a real, consistently-defined column — DDL in §3.1.4 + Drizzle in §7.1 — written at mint as intersect(requestedGrant, minter.allowedScopes) (NULL='*' stored only when the minter was '*'), read at resolve in the §7.2 bk_ branch (row.allowedScopes===null ? '*' : parseScopeGrant), with parseScopeGrant failing closed to [] on malformed input. A restricted key can never resolve to '*' and the one-step mint escalation is structurally closed. (2) trust_grade is sidecar-only (memory_use_policy), authoritatively NOT a Vectorize metadata index and NOT in the upsert blob (§3.2/§1.4/§5.2); foldPartitionFilter folds only scope/visibility, and the trust boost runs post-hydration on the LEFT-JOINed sidecar — no cross-grade leak via metadata. (3) Break-glass (§7.6) is role-gated (requireRole('admin')), fails CLOSED to 403 for non-admins (incl. breakGlass:true without the role), keeps tenant_id as a hard boundary, and writes a breakglass_read audit row in the same db.batch plus a guaranteed alert (canaries #14/#15). (4) The entity search arm (search_entities, §6.6/§6.7) now carries the same gate as the chunk arm: namespace=tenantId, scope+{world,team} visibility folded into the metadata filter, then an authoritative D1 re-check on entities via scopePredicate + {world,team} visibilityPredicate; the entities table actually carries scope/visibility/team_id columns (§6.1), and entities are partitioned by scope in the dedup key so 'Acme' under clientA vs clientB are two rows. The one material defect is an internal contradiction on the doc-graph link arm: §7.3's getLinks/expandFrontier gate at the EDGE level on docLinks.scope/entity_relations.scope — phantom columns absent from the §6.1 edge DDL — and return raw edge rows with NO node JOIN, while §6.1/§2110 and Flow C (§6.7) require the NODE-level scope+visibility gate on JOINed pages/entities endpoints. §7.4 compounds this with stale 'once graph nodes carry a visibility column... until then re-hydrate' prose that contradicts §6.1 (which already adds visibility to pages/entities). As literally coded in §7.3, get_links/get_backlinks under-gate to tenant_id only, leaking out-of-scope and team/private edge metadata + context text intra-tenant for a restricted Persona-C principal. The canonical traverse()/nodeGate/resolveScopedNode path is correct; the fix is to make getLinks/expandFrontier match it (node JOIN + nodeGate), which the spec must pick explicitly. A separate low-severity doc-hygiene miss: §1.5/§2/code-refs still say trust_grade is pushed 'to metadata'/'as metadata filters', contradicting the authoritative §3.2 — harmless to isolation (ranking only) but the sweep should scrub it.
